metadata.name: IRS CP3219A Statutory Notice of Deficiency Response
metadata.description: Respond to IRS CP3219A Statutory Notice of Deficiency — the 90-day letter. Opens the window to petition the U.S. Tax Court before paying the deficiency.

extraction.description: Extract data from CP90 Notice of Deficiency. This is a formal notice triggering appeal rights. Must extract all proposed adjustments, deficiency amount, and critical deadline for appeal petition.

fields.name: taxpayerName
fields.prompt: Extract taxpayer name from notice header.

fields.name: noticeDate
fields.prompt: Extract notice date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

fields.name: petitionDeadline
fields.prompt: Extract or calculate 90-day petition deadline from notice date.
fields.notes: CRITICAL: 90 days from notice date. After this, only payment/installment options remain.

fields.name: proposedAdjustments
fields.prompt: Extract all proposed adjustments with line numbers, amounts, and IRS reasoning.
fields.notes: Every line item must be addressed in response

fields.name: totalDeficiency
fields.prompt: Extract the total proposed deficiency (sum of all adjustments).

fields.name: serviceCenter
fields.prompt: Extract IRS Service Center that issued notice.

fields.name: appealRights
fields.prompt: Extract statement of taxpayer appeal rights. Look for language about Tax Court petition.
fields.example: You have the right to petition the Tax Court within 90 days of this notice
fields.notes: This is the critical legal notification triggering petition rights

extraction.notes: CP90 is the most formal IRS notice and triggers critical appeal rights. The 90-day Tax Court petition deadline is absolute and cannot be extended. Extraction must be extremely careful and accurate.

validation.description: Validate response strategy: protest deficiency, petition Tax Court, or negotiate settlement.

rules.name: petitionDeadlineCompliance
rules.message: If petitioning Tax Court, petition must be filed within 90 days of notice date. This is a strict, non-extendable deadline.
rules.example_fail: Notice dated August 15, 2024; Tax Court petition filed November 20, 2024 (outside 90-day window)
rules.example_pass: Notice dated August 15, 2024; Tax Court petition filed November 10, 2024 (within 90-day window)

rules.name: strategyChosen
rules.check: response indicates one of: (1) Tax Court petition, (2) Appeals Division protest, (3) payment/installment arrangement
rules.message: Response must indicate chosen strategy: dispute (via Tax Court or Appeals Division) or accept (with payment arrangement).
rules.example_fail: Response does not indicate taxpayer's chosen course of action
rules.example_pass: Response states: 'We intend to petition the Tax Court within 30 days' OR 'We respectfully request reconsideration by Appeals Division'

rules.name: allAdjustmentsAddressed
rules.message: Must address every proposed adjustment. Silence constitutes agreement.
rules.example_fail: Notice lists 4 adjustments; response only addresses 2
rules.example_pass: Response addresses all 4 adjustments with explanations

rules.name: supportingDocumentation
rules.message: If contesting adjustments, provide supporting documentation (W-2s, receipts, etc.)
rules.example_fail: Disputes wage amount but provides no W-2
rules.example_pass: Disputes wage amount and includes copy of Form W-2

rules.name: noLiabilityAdmission
rules.message: Do not admit error. Only state facts and provide evidence.
rules.example_fail: We admit we made a mistake...

rules.name: professionalFormat
rules.message: CP90 response must be formal business letter or formal Tax Court petition.
rules.example_pass: Formal letter with proper date, signature, and tax court letterhead if applicable

validation.notes: CP90 is critical. Response can either protest to Appeals Division or petition Tax Court. Wrong strategy or missed deadline can be irreversible.

aiPrompt.system: You are an expert tax attorney specializing in IRS examination procedures, appeals, and Tax Court petitions. You understand deficiency notices, appeal rights, and the critical 90-day petition deadline. Your role is to help taxpayers respond strategically to CP90 notices.
aiPrompt.task: Analyze the CP90 notice and determine the best response strategy: (1) Petition the Tax Court (strongest if deficiency is substantial), (2) Request Appeals Division review, or (3) Accept with installment agreement. Generate response consistent with chosen strategy.
aiPrompt.format: Formal business letter (protest strategy) or formal Tax Court petition (if litigation strategy chosen)
constraints: Never miss the 90-day petition deadline if choosing Tax Court strategy
Do not admit error or liability
Reference specific IRC sections and regulations only if applicable
Be clear about chosen strategy from first paragraph

examples.output: Formal Tax Court petition initiating litigation of deficiency with clear statement of disputed facts and legal arguments regarding wage income determination.

aiPrompt.notes: CP90 responses require careful strategic thinking. A wrong choice or missed deadline can be very costly. Consider hiring tax attorney.

responseTemplate.description: Formal response to CP90 Notice of Deficiency, either protesting to Appeals or petitioning Tax Court
responseTemplate.format: Formal business letter or Tax Court petition

sections.name: header
sections.template:
If protest: [IRS Appeals Division Address]
RE: Appeal of CP90 Notice of Deficiency
Tax Year [Year]
SSN: [XXX-XX-XXXX]

If Tax Court: U.S. Tax Court
400 2nd Street, NW
Washington, DC 20217

PETITION
RE: Petition of [Taxpayer Name] v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue
sections.guidance: Choose format based on strategy. Appeals = letter to service center. Tax Court = formal petition. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): If Tax Court; If protest.
sections.example:
U.S. Tax Court
400 2nd Street, NW
Washington, DC 20217

PETITION
RE: Petition of Robert James Wilson v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue

sections.name: statement_of_strategy
sections.template:
For protest: 'We respectfully request that this matter be reviewed by the Appeals Division and that the proposed deficiency be withdrawn or reduced based on the following arguments.'

For Tax Court: 'The Petitioner hereby petitions this Court to review and reverse the Notice of Deficiency issued on [date] for tax year [year].'
sections.guidance: Clear statement of taxpayer's chosen strategy from opening. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): For Tax Court; For protest.
sections.example: The Petitioner hereby petitions this Court to review and reverse the Notice of Deficiency issued on August 15, 2024 for tax year 2023.

sections.name: itemByItemResponse
sections.template:
For each proposed adjustment:
1. Restate IRS position
2. Explain taxpayer's position
3. Cite supporting evidence
4. Argue legal/factual basis for disagreement
sections.guidance: Methodical response to every adjustment. Must include factual and legal arguments.
sections.example:
ITEM 1: Wage Income for Tax Year 2023

IRS Position: Form W-2 from Employer ABC shows wages of $110,000.

Taxpayer Position: We reported $100,000 in wages, which reflects only compensation earned in 2023. The additional $10,000 represents a bonus paid in January 2024 and properly reportable in the 2024 tax year.

Supporting Evidence: Attached - Employer letter confirming bonus payment date; Copy of 2024 return showing bonus income.

Legal Basis: IRC Section 61 requires income to be reported in the year earned or received (cash method). The bonus was earned and received in 2024.

sections.name: prayer_for_relief
sections.template:
For protest: 'We respectfully request that the proposed deficiency be withdrawn or reduced based on the arguments and evidence presented above.'

For Tax Court: 'WHEREFORE, Petitioner respectfully requests that this Court determine that Petitioner is not liable for the deficiency set forth in the Notice of Deficiency issued on [date].'
sections.guidance: Formal closing requesting relief. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): For Tax Court; For protest.
sections.example: WHEREFORE, Petitioner respectfully requests that this Court determine that Petitioner is not liable for the deficiency set forth in the Notice of Deficiency issued on August 15, 2024.

sections.name: signature
sections.template:
Respectfully submitted,

[Signature]
[Typed Name]
[SSN]
[Address]

[Date]

Enclosures: [List of attached evidence]
sections.guidance: Formal legal-style signature block with all identifying information and date
sections.example:
Respectfully submitted,

Robert James Wilson
Robert James Wilson
SSN: 345-67-8901
123 Oak Avenue
Memphis, TN 38103

October 15, 2024

Enclosures:
- Letter from Employer ABC
- 2024 Tax Return (page 1)
- Bank statement showing bonus deposit

legalFramework.description: CP90 governed by IRC 6211 (notice of deficiency), IRC 6213 (restrictions on assessments and collections), and IRC 7422 (prohibited actions during deficiency period).
authorities: Internal Revenue Code Section 6211 - Notice of deficiency
Internal Revenue Code Section 6213 - Restrictions on assessments and collections during deficiency period
Internal Revenue Code Section 6214 - Determinations by Tax Court
Internal Revenue Code Section 7422 - Prohibition of suit prior to payment
Rules of the U.S. Tax Court (if pursuing Tax Court petition)
precedents: Taxpayer has 90 days from CP90 notice date to petition Tax Court
Tax Court petition suspends IRS collection activities
After 90-day period expires, only refund litigation option remains
Appeals Division review available as alternative to Tax Court
Burden of proof initially on IRS for most adjustments
criticalRules: The 90-day petition period is JURISDICTIONAL. The Tax Court cannot hear a late petition for any reason — not illness, not IRS delay, not an agreement between the parties.
Corresponding with the IRS during the 90 days does NOT extend it. Many taxpayers lose the window believing a phone call or letter paused the clock.
The date printed on the notice governs. IRC 6213(a) allows 150 days where the notice is addressed outside the United States.
Filing a petition suspends assessment and collection until the case is decided.
If the window is missed, the remaining route is to pay the deficiency and file a claim for refund, then sue in District Court or the Court of Federal Claims.

jurisdictionVariations.variation: CP90 procedures are purely federal and governed by IRC. No state tax variations.

cases.name: cp90-appeals-strategy
cases.description: CP90 with moderate deficiency, response via Appeals Division
cases.inputDocument: CP90 notice with $15,000 deficiency from wage adjustment
cases.expectedResponse: Letter to Appeals Division explaining why wage adjustment is incorrect with supporting evidence
successCriteria: Clearly states Appeals Division protest strategy

cases.name: cp90-tax-court-strategy
cases.description: CP90 with substantial deficiency, response via Tax Court petition
cases.expectedResponse: Formal Tax Court petition within 90-day deadline with complete factual and legal arguments
successCriteria: Tax Court petition filed to correct court

relatedWorkflows.description: Workflows related to CP90 deficiency response

implementation.notes: CP90 is the most formal and critical IRS notice. It triggers federal court jurisdiction and the 90-day petition deadline is absolute. This workflow is high-complexity and should be handled with extreme care.
knownChallenges: The 90-day deadline is non-extendable and triggers strict procedural requirements
Distinguishing between Appeals Division and Tax Court strategies
Following Tax Court procedural and substantive requirements
Handling complex factual disputes that may require expert testimony
